recipes.name: Nadine's Delicious Tilapia
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds tilapia fillets, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps.text: Beat the egg and soy sauce together in a bowl.

Gently press the tilapia pieces into the flour to coat; shake off the excess flour. Dip each flour-coated piece into the beaten egg mixture and then press into bread crumbs. Gently toss between your hands so any bread crumbs that haven't stuck can fall away. Place the breaded tilapia onto a plate while breading the rest; do not stack.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the breaded tilapia in the vegetable oil until golden brown, about 5 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Nadine's Delicious Tilapia
raw_recipe.description: Beating soy sauce with the egg before breading the tilapia adds flavor to this simple, pan-fried fish recipe.

review.reviewBody: Excellent fish, crusty and not at all greasy! I added parmesan cheese to the bread crumbs, and cooked in 1/2 sesame oil and 1/2 vegetable oil. I'll definitely make this again.

Hubby didn't really like the breading-then again I used gluten free bread crumbs and made the addition of the Parmesan cheese as suggested. Instead of using flour I used cornstarch before breading. With the cornstarch the breading stuck awesomely!

These were the best fried fish I've ever made! The breading stayed on, and had a good flavor. I used panko bread crumbs, because that's what I had, and put some salt-free seasoning in them. The soy sauce has plenty of salt in it. I'll use this same breading on other meats, and maybe try it on fried or baked tofu.

Great dish!! I did not cut into pieces. Cooked stovetop in EVOO. I used flavored croutons and crushed them in a bag for my 'bread crumbs'. Added salt to the flour and Garlic Powder and Garlic Salt, Pepper and Itailian Season to the bread crumbs. NOTE - pat the fish dry before putting in flour. Flour will hold to the better and hold the crumbs better!

Made this recipe for the family and it went over very well. As suggested by others I added some Panko, used lite soy sauce, added some sesame oil to the soy/egg mixture and added parmesan cheese. Delicious! Thank you for the recipe. Oh, I also dried the tilapia before running it through the flour. This did make the flour stay on the fish.
This was great!!!! I used olive oil instead of vegetable oil, and panko breadcrumbs. It was so tasty for tilapia which usually doesn't have a tremendous amount of flavor. I will make again for sure.

Great basic recipe for tilapia. I used a special teriyaki sauce in place of the soy sauce and added fresh lemon juice with the egg/teriyaki mixture. I used Panko bread crumbs with my homemade seasoning and a little chopped fresh parsley. Fried in avocado oil.

I don't like fish all that much but my family loves it so I have been searching for a recipe that I can tolerate so I don't have to make a separate dinner on fish nights. Well, this fish is delicious! I never thought I would say that but I honestly can't wait to make it again. I fried the fish then put it straight onto a baking sheet and put them in the oven to finish cooking through. I cooked them low (about 200) for at least an hour if not more. they were perfect! I served it with the bacon fried rice recipe I got off this website. it was a hit! The kids asked if I could make it again tomorrow.
This was the best tilapia recipe I have had so far I loved it the only thing I added to it was a quarter cup of Parmesan cheese to the the breading

is was so quick and easy to make and very tasty! I loved the light crispy coating. It was not greasy at all. I didn't even have soy sauce and it was still delicious. I added some garlic powder, Lawry's Seasoned Salt and some pepper. I was in such a hurry to make dinner I didn't read where it said to cut the tilapia into 2-inch pieces. I just heated the oil and dipped the whole fillets in flour, egg and the bread crumbs. I just added a few extra minutes until the fish flaked easily with a fork. Next time I will try with the soy sauce, but I loved this without it. Thanks for a delicious and easy recipe!
Whole family loved it; even my daughter who doesn’t like fish. Used olive oil instead of vegetable oil and added sesame oil to the egg wash as others recommended.
Made per directions and my honey said it was the best he has had. I thought it was yummy too. Very simple to make. I also used the Tangy (Not Sweet) Tarter Sauce recipe and it was amazing as well.

I actually hate fish but am trying to incorporate it into my diet. I tried this out and absolutely loved it! It wasn’t fishy at all, had a good flavor & texture. (I used more italian bread crumbs than it called for & used some sweet chili sauce on the side)
Turned out great. My husband said it was the best Tilapia I have ever fixed.
Very good! Loved the light crispness over the flaky flesh. I'll try with panko and play with the seasoning next time.
Made it with haddock and it was exceptional. Only change made was using panko instead of breadcrumbs and adding a bit of shredded Parm cheese. One of my favorites!
I added some seasoning to the bread crumbs and sesame seed oil to the egg wash as per other users suggestions it was delicious and so easy
I may use 2 eggs next time
While this was nice and crispy, we both felt it lacked flavor, and we also felt as if it needed some kind of sauce.
I just added a couple of cloves of garlic to the sauce and used Panko bread crumbs. It was delicious.
